title: Motorcyclists
whatItIs: Motorcyclists are hard to see, especially at junctions, and may be closer and faster than you think. Look out for them and give them room.
keyFacts: Motorcyclists are hard to see at junctions, at roundabouts and when filtering: look carefully.
They may filter between lanes of slow or stopped traffic: check your mirrors before you change lane.
A rider looking over their shoulder may be about to turn or change lane: give them time.
Riders may swerve suddenly to avoid potholes, drain covers or slippery patches.
In strong wind, keep well back from motorcyclists overtaking large vehicles.

items.title: At junctions
items.text: They may be closer and faster than you think. Look carefully.

items.title: Filtering
items.text: Bikes may pass between lanes of slow traffic. Check mirrors.

items.title: Shoulder checks
items.text: A rider looking back may be about to move. Give them space.

items.title: Bad road surfaces
items.text: Potholes and drain covers can make a rider swerve.

b.label: Indicator flashing
points: Wait to see what they do

onTheTest.question: Why should you look carefully for motorcyclists at junctions?
options: They are hard to see and may be faster than you think
They must stop at every junction
They are not allowed to filter
onTheTest.why: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They may be closer and faster than you expect, so look carefully before you pull out.

traps: Motorcyclists are hard to see: check mirrors and blind spots carefully before you turn or pull out.
Filtering motorcyclists can pass on either side.
A rider may swerve for a drain cover or pothole: leave room.
